## ADS-IDAC now runs anywhere, and much faster {#perf-workstation data-section="5"}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="59%"}
![](figs/walltime_steps.svg){fig-align="center" width="100%" fig-alt="Wall time of one benchmark run as the four factors are added. On an 8-core workstation: 752 s for the original engine, 193 s with the serial optimizations, 81 s with a modern toolchain. On a 14-core laptop: 21.4 s on one core, 4.8 s with MPI parallelism"}
:::
::: {.column width="41%"}
```{=html}
<div class="eq"><div class="eq-total"><b>156×</b><span><strong>752&nbsp;s</strong> to <strong>4.8&nbsp;s</strong>:<br>the same benchmark run, end to end</span></div></div>
```

::: {style="font-size:0.86em;"}
[**The engine now runs efficiently on a laptop or a workstation.**]{style="color:#B40000;"}

- **The 156× is conservative.** The 752 s baseline was timed on a modern
  workstation with an SSD.
- **Parallelism pays more on realistic scenarios.** This benchmark tree is
  small; larger trees gain more.
:::
:::
::::

::: {.notes}
What does all of this buy? ADS-IDAC now runs efficiently on a laptop or a
workstation, and much faster.

The chart follows one benchmark run. The original engine took seven hundred
fifty-two seconds on a workstation. Serial optimizations bring that to a
hundred ninety-three, and a modern toolchain to eighty-one. On a fourteen-core
laptop the same run takes twenty-one seconds on one core, and four point eight
on ten ranks. End to end, that is a hundred fifty-six times faster.

And that comparison is conservative: the seven hundred fifty-two seconds were
timed on a modern workstation with a solid-state disk, so the original setup
was slower still.

This benchmark tree is small. On more realistic scenarios, with many more
sequences, parallelism pays off even more.
:::

sequences, and a hundred sixty-nine thousand pivotal events.

On the right, a more realistic scenario on the same plant, in a tree designed
to be wide and deep: thirty-five thousand six hundred sequences in one hour of
mission time, and more than eleven million pivotal events.

The picture is a sample of that second tree. Every line is a full plant
transient with a simulated crew.

## Generated efficiently: days of computing become under an hour {#large-trees-efficiency data-section="5"}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="57%"}
![](figs/tree_ladder.svg){fig-align="center" width="100%" fig-alt="Time to build the 35,000-sequence tree against MPI ranks, on log axes. On 32-core Intel nodes: 15.1 h at 32 ranks, 7.3 h at 64, 3.7 h at 128, 1.9 h at 256. On 192-core AMD nodes: 1.3 h at 256 ranks, 40 min at 512, 27 min at 768. Both follow their ideal lines"}
:::
::: {.column width="43%"}
```{=html}
<div class="plates"><div class="plate p2">
  <div class="p-sub">the 35,000-sequence tree, start to finish</div>
  <div class="p-nums">
    <div><div class="p-num">12.5 days</div><div class="p-lab">one core, projected</div></div>
    <div class="go">→</div>
    <div><div class="p-num">58.6 min</div><div class="p-lab">one job, 512 ranks</div></div>
  </div>
</div></div>
```

::: {style="font-size:0.86em; margin-top:0.5em;"}
[**A gigantic tree is one cluster job of under an hour.**]{style="color:#B40000;"}

- **Scaling stays near ideal:** 94 to 98% up to 768 ranks.
- **The 12,306-sequence tree** converges in 57 minutes on 768 ranks, and a
  second run reproduces it exactly.
:::
:::
::::

::: {.notes}
And generating these trees is efficient.

The chart shows the time to build the larger tree, about thirty-five thousand
sequences, on a cluster. Each time the number of ranks doubles, the time
halves, all the way to seven hundred sixty-eight ranks. That is ninety-four to
ninety-eight percent of ideal scaling.

On one core, this tree would take about twelve and a half days. On five
hundred twelve ranks, the whole study is one job of under an hour.

The tube-rupture tree converges in fifty-seven minutes on seven hundred
sixty-eight ranks, and a second, independent run reproduced it exactly.

At this scale, the point is not that a tree is faster to generate. It is that
it can be generated at all.
:::
